# Actual registered signed loopback / synthetic PostgreSQL receipts

All six `registered-*.json` files are the original response bytes from the real `sales.urls` consumer_query route, HMAC principal verification and owning SQL reader, on a dynamic loopback Django LiveServer and a private synthetic PostgreSQL. They were captured by the dedicated author run `crossdomain-pg-02900ce698bff96f` at source HEAD `73f23edbfb0b4d348e408175607a86e9fc4d7d58` plus dedicated Python adapter validation and test drafts. No business values were composed by this fixture adapter. Matching meta files retain request, allowed response headers, byte count and SHA. Authentication headers/internal secrets are excluded.

The same run made five actual TS SDK HTTP calls to this private registered endpoint: success, actual typed version 409, absent-actor 403, invalid-signature 401 and actual 403 followed by cancellation returning 499. That evidence remains external `capacity/actual-ts-sdk-result.json`; `capacity/actual-http-lifecycle.json` binds source hashes before/after, reports sourceStable and normal HTTP thread closure. The private PG also stopped normally. These are author checks, not independent Q or production source/adoption evidence.

Fixtures cover unrestricted full facts, four-role exact channel+warehouse reads, raw whitespace under an explicit native platform+warehouse scope, genuine typed zero, missing trusted ERP order numbers, and >500 baseline-only candidates while search/page do not alter the whole two-period totals. Under a channel-only grant, raw whitespace is not an alias and correctly returns no rows; the existing permission rules are unchanged. Observed imported dates remain unknown completeness. Cost/profit primary use remains unavailable or partial with unverified_source, even when stored amounts are zero.

Replay tests use the real TS decoder/SDK and Python dedicated adapter on these immutable receipts. Only the author live probe inside the owned PG test opens network connections, guarded to that selected dynamic loopback endpoint. Replays are synthetic transports; they do not pretend to be live data. The final source/test commit and file hashes are recorded in the external delivery manifest. Earlier failed harness runs with API-only STATIC_URL/MEDIA_URL None remain preserved separately; only test settings were adapted to inert static/media prefixes, never fetched.
